name: Stihl MS 170 / MS 180
blurb: Stihl's entry-level saws. Stock 16″ setup: 3/8″ Picco low-profile, .043″ gauge, 55 drive links — Stihl 61 PMM3.
intro: The MS 170 and MS 180 (including C-BE variants) are Stihl's lightest homeowner saws, sold with 12″, 14″ and — most commonly in recent years — 16″ bars. All use Stihl's Picco Micro Mini low-profile chain in .043″ gauge. The 16″ specification below is confirmed from the OEM chain listing; the shorter bars share the pitch and gauge but not the drive-link count, which is why we list the 16″ row as fact and point the other lengths at your bar stamp.

sources.title: OEM part 3610 005 0055 — 61 PMM3 55 (3/8″ pitch, .043″ gauge, 55 drive links; fitments include MS 170, MS 171, MS 180, MS 181)
Cross-references naming Oregon 90PX, Carlton N4C and Husqvarna H38 equivalents

sources_note: 16″ spec from a Stihl dealer listing of OEM part 3610 005 0055 (61 PMM3 55: 3/8″ pitch, .043″ gauge, 55 drive links; fitments include MS 170, MS 171, MS 180, MS 181) and cross-reference listings naming Oregon 90PX, Carlton N4C and Husqvarna H38 equivalents — checked Oct 2026.

bars.note: The stock fitment for current MS 170 / MS 180 saws. Discontinued pre-2023 examples on the older .050″ Picco setup exist — if your stamp reads .050″ / 1.3 mm, your chain is the 63 PM3 type instead.
Both lengths were factory options. We have not traced their drive-link counts to an OEM listing we can cite, so we do not print a number — the stamp on the bar tail states it.
